item.title: Currency outside banks rises 104% in 3 yrs — CBN
item.description: •Demand deposits climb 71% •Analysts highlight cash dependence, financial inclusion challenges By Peter Egwuatu Currency held outside the banking system by Nigerians rose by 103.8 per cent to N4.923 trillion in September 2026 from N2.416 trillion in September 2023, highlighting the persistent demand for physical cash despite the expansion of electronic payment channels in the country. Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, Money and Credit Statistics, also showed that currency outside banks increased by 10.3 per cent year-on-year from N4.465 trillion in September 2025 to N4.923 trillion in September 2026. The figures indicate that cash held outside the banking system has more than doubled in three years, reflecting the scale of currency demand within the economy and the challenges facing efforts to deepen the use of formal banking and electronic payment systems. A breakdown of the data showed that currency outside banks increased by 66.2 per cent from N2.416 trillion in September 2023 to N4.016 trillion in September 2024. The figure subsequently rose to N4.465 trillion in September 2025, an increase of 11.2 per cent from the corresponding period in 2024, before climbing further to N4.923 trillion in September 2026. According to analysts, the latest increase indicates that the preference for cash transactions remains significant, notwithstanding the growing adoption of mobile banking, electronic transfers, point-of-sale terminals and other digital payment platforms. Demand deposits rise 71% Meanwhile, demand deposits in the banking system increased by 70.8 per cent to N39.124 trillion in September 2026 from N22.903 trillion in September 2023. The CBN data showed that demand deposits rose to N31.842 trillion in September 2024, representing an increase of 39.0 per cent against the corresponding period in 2023. The figure climbed further to N34.642 trillion in September 2025, an increase of 8.8 per cent year-on-year, before rising to N39.124 trillion in September 2026, representing a 12.9 per cent increase over September 2025. The growth in demand deposits indicates an expansion in funds held in bank accounts that are generally accessible for payments and withdrawals on demand. Reacting to this data, Clifford Egbomeade, Economic and Communications expert, said: “The simultaneous increase in demand deposits and currency outside banks points to the coexistence of formal banking balances and substantial demand for physical cash in Nigeria’s payment system. ‘‘However, the two indicators measure different components of monetary activity. Demand deposits represent bank-account balances, while currency outside banks represents cash held outside the banking system. ‘‘Their growth rates alone do not establish how much of the increase in cash holdings is attributable to economic growth, inflation, informal transactions or changes in payment preferences.” Vanguard News The post Currency outside banks rises 104% in 3 yrs — CBN appeared first on Vanguard New

item.title: Women in Politics: Nigeria’s political structure not built for women — Adeola Azeez
item.description: By Ebunoluwa Sessou As Nigeria prepares for another general election in 2027, the question of women’s participation in politics and access to elective offices remains a subject for debate. Read Also: Elections: INEC struggles to get 14m PVCs to voters Adeola Azeez, a daughter of the late Afenifere leader, Pa Ayo Adebanjo and one of the Founders of Women in Management, Business & Public Service, WIMBIZ, a founding member of Women in Politics (WIMPol) and a former Deputy Country Representative, Nigeria, of Deutsch e-Bank; was recently declared winner at the Ijebu Central Federal Consistency primary election on the platform of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) in Ogun State. In this interview, she speaks on her experience contesting for the House of Representatives, the challenges of securing a party ticket, the influence of party structures on women’s political ambitions and her determination to contest again in 2027. She also discusses the need for women who have secured elective positions to support aspiring female politicians and explains why she believes women must remain committed to political participation despite the barriers they face. Excerpts: You transitioned from the corporate world to politics after your retirement in 2020. What informed that decision? I have always believed in the importance of women’s participation in leadership. By the time I retired in 2020, I had prepared myself for a career in politics. From 2013, I knew that politics was something I wanted to pursue, so I began preparing for it. I eventually contested for the House of Representatives in 2023 to represent Ogbomoso Central Federal Constituency. I approached the contest with the same seriousness, preparation and determination as any other candidate. What were the major challenges you encountered as a woman contesting for political office? The challenges women face in politics are well known. They include political violence, limited access to funding and other barriers. Interestingly, funding was not a major challenge for me because of my corporate experience and the relationships I had built over the years. Having supported, mentored and nurtured women in business, I had established a strong network of sponsors and supporters. My reputation also helped me attract people who believed in my ambition. However, the major challenge was the political structure itself. Nigeria’s political system is not structured to accommodate women adequately. Despite your corporate experience, network and supporters, you did not secure your party’s ticket in 2023. What went wrong? I believe the challenge was the party structure and the people who control access to political opportunities. I had expected that my pedigree, experience and contributions to society would count for something. I did my research, reached out to my constituency and carried out the necessary groundwork. item.title: 2027: Tinubu inherited Nigeria on brink of collapse — Mutfwang
item.description: •Declares no vacancy in Aso Rock, Plateau Govt House •Says no rainbow coalition, Plateau going APC By Golok Nanmwa JOS — Plateau State governor, Caleb Mutfwang, has said President Bola Tinubu inherited an economy that was tottering on the brink of collapse from the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari in 2023. Read Also: Elections: INEC struggles to get 14m PVCs to voters He also declared there was no vacancy in the Presidential Villa (Aso Rock) and Plateau Government House in 2027, equally dismissing any talks of rainbow coalition. Mutfwang, who stated this during the formal inauguration of All Progressives Congress, APC, Campaign Council in Jos yesterday, also defended Tinubu administration’s economic reforms and urged Plateau residents to support the President in the 2027 election. “Where did President Tinubu meet Nigeria in 2023? He met Nigeria tottering on the brink of collapse; Nigeria that could not service its external debts; Nigeria that would not even allow businesses outside the country to take their proceeds back home. And that is why some international airlines stopped flying to Nigeria because they could not get the dollars to take back their money. “Our external reserve was down to just a little over $3 billion, from the over $40 billion it had accumulated for decades. Today, by the grace of God, we have a healthy external reserve of over $50 billion,” the governor said. He alleged further that the previous administration resorted to printing money to manage the economy, claiming more than N30 trillion was printed. Governor Mutfwang said: “When the President took over in 2023, the government he succeeded had run out of ideas on how to manage the economy and they resorted to printing money in the Central Bank. “They printed over N30 trillion which went down the drain. Today, by the grace of God, Central Bank has stabilised and that deficit has been done away with.’’ On fuel subsidy, Mutfwang described the system under the previous administration as fraudulent, alleging that the country borrowed money to pay claims supported by what he called fictitious documents. “I say it was a fraud because we were borrowing money to pay people who brought fictitious documents. They never brought any wealth. They brought fictitious documents, claimed monies and subsidies. “You cannot continue to borrow money to give to thieves. You have to stop it at some point. And when it is stopped, there will be a payback; there will be a recovery time,” he said. The governor said the availability of fuel had improved, despite the increase in its cost, recalling the long queues that previously characterised fuel stations across the country. “Today, by the grace of God, we have solved one side of the equation. Today, fuel is available. It may not be cheap but it is available. “Those of us who are of my age bracket or little below will remember the times we spent days in petrol stations queuing for fuel that we could hardly get. item.title: Give Tinubu, Otu another term for Bakassi seaport, coastal highway — Shettima
item.description: By Ike Uchechukwu CALABAR — Vice President Kashim Shettima has assured Cross River residents that the proposed Bakassi Deep Seaport and Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway will be delivered, urging them to re-elect President Bola Tinubu and Governor Bassey Otu in 2027. Shettima gave the assurance yesterday while representing Tinubu at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally at the U.J. Esuene Stadium, Calabar. He thanked the people of Cross River for supporting the administration over the past three years, describing the relationship between the government and the electorate as “an alliance of prosperity, an alliance of opportunity.” “Over the past three years, you have shown us support, and you have resisted the lies and propaganda intended to misrepresent us,” he said. The Vice President urged voters to renew the mandates of Tinubu, Otu and APC candidates seeking election into the National Assembly and the state House of Assembly. He said the party was seeking another mandate based on its stewardship, stressing that elected officials must account to the people who entrusted them with power. On infrastructure, Shettima said the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway would link coastal communities, ease the movement of goods and people, boost tourism and attract investment to the region. He added that the project would create thousands of direct and indirect jobs, while opening up economic opportunities for communities along the corridor. On the Bakassi Deep Seaport, the Vice President said the project had received Federal Government approval, expressing optimism that it would become an international maritime gateway upon completion. “When completed, it will become an international maritime gateway. It will attract shipping companies. It will generate employment,” he said. Shettima said the seaport and coastal highway were central to efforts to position Cross River as a major beneficiary of Nigeria’s maritime economy. On education, he said the government’s student financing initiative would promote human capital development, reduce the financial burden on parents and expand access to higher education. item.title: FG disburses N75bn to 104 manufacturers, N65.8bn to MSMEs
item.description: By Yinka Kolawole The Federal Government has fully disbursed the N75 billion Manufacturing Sector Fund to 104 manufacturing businesses, while N65.8 billion has been disbursed to 15,018 micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to boost domestic production, expand businesses and create jobs. Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment, Dr Jumoke Oduwole, disclosed this in an address on “Harnessing Nigeria’s Economic Potential for Greater Prosperity”. Oduwole said the interventions were part of the Federal Government’s efforts to strengthen local industries, improve productive capacity and drive sustainable economic growth. The disbursements were made under the Federal Government’s N200 billion intervention package, managed by the Bank of Industry (BoI), to support businesses, boost domestic production and create jobs. The package comprises the N50 billion Presidential Conditional Grant Scheme for nano businesses, the N75 billion FGN MSME Intervention Fund for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, and the N75 billion FGN Manufacturing Sector Fund for manufacturing businesses. Oduwole noted that the N75 billion Manufacturing Sector Fund had been fully disbursed to 104 manufacturing businesses, while N65.8 billion had been disbursed to 15,018 businesses under the MSME Intervention Fund as of the first quarter of 2026. She, however, stressed that the impact of government funding should be measured by stronger businesses, increased production and improved livelihoods rather than the amount disbursed alone. The minister acknowledged that access to finance remained a major challenge for manufacturers seeking to acquire equipment, purchase raw materials, expand production capacity and create employment. She said Nigeria’s economic transformation required fiscal discipline, monetary stability and policies that supported domestic production and competitiveness. According to her, the government is working to remove barriers to investment, production and trade while creating an enabling environment for businesses to thrive. Highlighting developments in the manufacturing sector, Oduwole said cement manufacturing grew by 11.53 per cent in the first quarter of 2026, while motor vehicle assembly expanded by 5.44 per cent during the period. She added that vehicle assembly grew by 40.6 per cent in 2025, while cassava starch production recorded growth of 474.74 per cent. “Processing locally grown cassava into industrial starch will support manufacturers, while vehicle assembly will create opportunities for engineers, technicians and supply-chain businesses,” she said. The minister also highlighted opportunities under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), noting that intra-African trade had grown by 21 per cent. item.title: YPP’s Agada wants end to raw material exports
item.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA — The presidential candidate of the Young Progressives Party (YPP), Arch. Peter Agada, has called for an end to the export of Nigeria’s raw materials without adding value, saying the practice deprives the country of greater economic benefits. Agada spoke in an interview in Abuja on Monday while outlining his economic blueprint ahead of the 2027 general elections. He said his proposed administration would prioritise electricity supply and promote industrialisation from the ward level to ensure that value was added to Nigerian produce before export. “The industrialisation we all talk about can only happen when we fix power and put in place policies that will promote investments from the ward level upwards,” Agada said. He said rural communities would be made attractive to agro-allied industries capable of processing agricultural produce for export and generating foreign exchange. “Our rural communities will attract agro-allied industries to promote export of produce after value has been added to earn foreign exchange. Enough of sending raw materials only to collect peanuts in return,” he said. The YPP candidate also said his proposed administration would mobilise Nigerians at home and in the diaspora to build a country citizens would be proud to call home. He said this would involve building on the country’s strengths while addressing areas of weakness. On politics, Agada urged members of the political elite, irrespective of party affiliation, to allow Nigerians to freely choose their leaders at all levels. He said the practice of imposing leaders on the electorate on the basis of ethnic or religious considerations should become a thing of the past. item.title: Customs appoints Mamman Ali acting Adamawa/Taraba Comptroller
item.description: By Umar Yusuf, Yola The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) has appointed Deputy Comptroller Mamman Ali as the Acting Area Comptroller of its Adamawa/Taraba Command. Ali, who was until his appointment the Coordinator of the Customs Anti-Smuggling Unit, Operation Whirlwind, Zone E, takes over from Mohammed Tako, who has been promoted to Assistant Comptroller-General of Customs in charge of Zone B, Kaduna. At a brief handing-over ceremony in Yola on Monday, Tako said the command recorded significant achievements during his tenure despite directives on strict border closure. He said the command strengthened security along critical border corridors through enhanced joint operations and patrols with sister security agencies. Tako disclosed that the total Duty Paid Value (DPV) of seizures recorded by the command during his one-year tenure stood at ₦535,975,190. He commended officers and men of the command for their cooperation during his tenure and urged them to extend the same support to his successor. In his remarks, the new Acting Area Comptroller, Ali, pledged to build on the achievements of his predecessor. He solicited the support and cooperation of sister security agencies, officers and men of the command to strengthen border policing and curb smuggling activities across Adamawa and Taraba states. item.title: Ogun 2027: Adebutu dismisses INEC list omission
item.description: ….Receives over 1,000 APC defectors into PDP By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta ABEOKUTA — The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ogun State, Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu, has described the omission of his name from the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) list of governorship candidates as a temporary distraction, insisting that it would not stop him from contesting the 2027 election. Adebutu spoke on Monday while receiving more than 1,000 defectors from the All Progressives Congress (APC) into the PDP at the party’s state secretariat in Abeokuta. The defectors were led by a former member of the House of Representatives, Hon. Segun William, and received by Adebutu alongside other party leaders, including the PDP’s Ogun Central senatorial candidate, Iyabo Obasanjo. Addressing the gathering, Adebutu expressed confidence that the controversy surrounding his omission from INEC’s list would be resolved, maintaining that he remained a bona fide member of the PDP. He cited his participation in elections under the party’s platform over the past two decades as evidence of his loyalty and challenged those questioning his membership to provide evidence that he had defected. “I have been the candidate of the PDP for the last 20 years, in every election cycle. My question is: at what stage did I leave or vacate the party? Where is the proof that, for one day, I have even visited the APC office, let alone joined the party?” he asked. Adebutu also said he played an active role in organising and financing the party’s recent membership registration exercise in Ogun, which he claimed recorded more than 19,800 members. He said his registration number in the exercise was 1536, describing it as further evidence of his continued membership of the party. The PDP chieftain alleged that the controversy over his omission from the INEC list was intended to distract the opposition and disenfranchise voters. He, however, urged party members to remain focused, saying the development would not disrupt the PDP’s mobilisation activities across the state. Adebutu disclosed that the party’s campaign team had visited 12 of the state’s 20 local government areas and more than 140 of its 236 wards. He said the grassroots mobilisation exercise would continue despite what he described as attempts to distract the party. “We have visited 12 of the 20 local governments. Of the 236 wards, we have visited over 140. Tomorrow, we continue again because we know that the trick is to get us distracted. We will not be distracted. We will keep our eyes on the ball, and we shall win,” he said. Earlier, William said the defectors decided to leave the APC because of their dissatisfaction with the party’s approach to governance and what he described as its failure to uphold democratic principles and deliver development in Ogun State. item.title: Diri urges Bayelsa governorship aspirants to seek God
item.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa YENAGOA — Governor Douye Diri of Bayelsa State has urged anyone aspiring to succeed him to seek God’s approval through prayer, saying the next governor must be a God-fearing person. Diri spoke on Monday during the state’s 15th Thanksgiving service at the Ecumenical Centre, Igbogene, Yenagoa, where he declared that Bayelsa had been handed over to God. He said nobody could stop anyone chosen by God to lead the state, adding that the Almighty would always have the final say in its affairs. The governor also urged residents to remain united, tolerant and peaceful, describing these as essential conditions for the state’s development. He reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to improving the lives of residents, saying it had the political will to transform Bayelsa, which he described as one of the states with the best environments for development. Diri thanked the people for their support over the past six years and urged them to sustain their cooperation with the government. “All who want to be governor, go and seek the face of God. Anyone who wants to be governor must be God-fearing. If God said yes, nobody can say no, not even me,” he said. He added: “Let us continue to worship God. Let us be tolerant and patient as we will become victorious at the end of the day. “As I keep saying, those of us who were born in Yenagoa or know Bayelsa of old can see the difference today. It is enough to give thanks. “We have one of the best environments in Nigeria, and with the political will, we are bringing development to our people.” In his sermon, the guest preacher and former Bayelsa State Chairman of the Christian Association of Nigeria, Very Rev. Joseph Opelema, urged Christians to combine their religious faith with responsible citizenship. Speaking on the theme, “Called to be Good Christians and Good Citizens,” Opelema said Christians had dual responsibilities as members of the church and citizens of society. Drawing his message from Matthew 22:15-22, where Jesus addressed the question of paying taxes, he said the biblical instruction to give to Caesar what belongs to Caesar and to God what belongs to God underscored the importance of responsible citizenship. The cleric said Christians should demonstrate sacrifice, prudence, accountability, justice, love, care and charity wherever they found themselves, particularly in public office. He lamented what he described as a gap between religious participation and the practice of Christian values, urging believers to become witnesses, the salt of the earth and the light of the world. Opelema also described Bayelsa as richly endowed with natural and human resources, favourable weather, land and rivers, which he said could make the state a tourism destination. He expressed optimism that the state could realise its potential with God-fearing leadership. item.title: North Korea slams FBI allegations over Binance hack as ‘grave’ provocation
item.description: North Korea on Tuesday slammed the FBI’s allegations that Pyongyang was behind the theft of $6 billion from cryptocurrency platform Binance, with Kim Jong Un’s powerful sister labelling it a “grave political provocation”. Kim Yo Jong, in a statement released Tuesday by the KCNA state news agency, said the FBI’s claim was “absurd rhetoric and nothing new,” given prior US allegations that North Korea was behind last year’s major hack of Bybit. “It is a grave political provocation against the DPRK that the US misleads the international public opinion as if all the cyber crimes in different parts of the world are our deeds,” Kim said, using the acronym for North Korea’s official name. The FBI said on Saturday that a North Korea-affiliated hacking group called TraderTraitor had been behind the hack. TraderTraitor is the same group blamed for a $1.5 billion theft from the Bybit platform in February last year, which had been the largest crypto theft until the Binance hack. “This is a sinister attempt to damage the international image of the DPRK and undermine its dignity and national prestige and another grave violation of the sovereignty of the DPRK,” Kim said. “It is the consistent policy stand of the DPRK government to resolutely oppose all sorts of malicious acts in cyberspace,” she added. Binance is the world’s largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes. News of the hacking attack caused the prices of most major cryptocurrencies to fall sharply on Friday. After the FBI released its statement on Saturday, US President Donald Trump cast doubt on North Korea’s involvement in the hack. “I’m not concerned. We’re learning about it. We don’t know if it’s North Korea,” Trump told reporters at his residence in Florida. Trump has made repeated overtures to nuclear-armed North Korea since returning to office, and said he was open to meeting with supreme leader Kim Jong Un this year. Those gestures have been met with silence from Pyongyang. Kim Yo Jong, in her statement, said the new allegations “confirmed Washington’s hostile attitude toward the DPRK once again.” “We have issues to reconsider in diverse aspects as regards the very unpleasant US hostile attitude,” she added. item.title: Critics of Rainbow Coalition can’t unite their families – Wike
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi – ABUJA Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has said politicians who deny the existence of the Rainbow Coalition lack the capacity to unite even their own families and communities. Read Also: 2027: Obi couldn’t fix Anambra; Atiku will return to Dubai after election — Oshiomhole Wike spoke on Monday in Abuja at the commissioning of the Gwagwalada Civic Centre and an interactive session with stakeholders of the All Progressives Congress APC and the Peoples Democratic Party PDP in Gwagwalada Area Council. The minister said the coalition, which brings together political stakeholders from both parties, was formed in the interest of unity, cooperation and development in the FCT. “Some greedy and selfish politicians do not understand what we call unity. They have no capacity to hold their space, they have no capacity to even hold their families, and they have no capacity to hold their communities. So they can open their mouths and say there is no Rainbow Coalition,” he said. Wike challenged critics of the alliance to explain why political leaders who once disagreed could not come together to pursue common interests. He described the development in Gwagwalada as a departure from the politics of confrontation, insisting that the FCT needed cooperation rather than needless political hostility. Commending political leaders in the area for setting aside their differences, he said their decision showed that the collective interest of the people outweighed individual political ambition. Wike also urged residents not to repeat what he described as the mistake of the 2023 general elections, and called for credible representation at the National Assembly. The minister canvassed support for a former senator, Philip Aduda, and other candidates endorsed by the coalition, saying political representatives must be accessible and familiar with their constituents. Wike also declared support for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and urged residents to turn their endorsements into votes in 2027. “On the day of the election, it will not be a day for market or fishing. It is the day all of us have decided to come together and demonstrate our strength through our votes. Go to the polling units, districts and communities and mobilise the people to vote for Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said. APC chair Earlier, the FCT APC Chairman, Ishaku Tanko Yamawo, described the gathering as historic, saying Wike’s intervention had brought together leaders who previously operated on opposing sides. The FCT PDP Chairman, Alhaji Ismaila Mohammed Dogara, praised Wike for his development interventions, particularly the revival of a project abandoned for 16 years in Gwagwalada. The Aguma of Gwagwalada, Alhaji Muhammadu Magaji, also commended Wike’s contributions to the development of the territory. item.title: EPL: Everton deepen Newcastle crisis with 1-0 win
item.description: Everton increased the pressure on under-fire Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle as Thierno Barry sealed a 1-0 win at St James’ Park on Monday. Barry netted early in the second half to lift Everton into seventh place in the Premier League and leave Newcastle languishing in 13th. Newcastle midfielder Jacob Ramsey was sent off in the final seconds for a crude foul on Harrison Armstrong. It was a fitting end to another painful defeat for Saudi-funded Newcastle, who have lost four of their past five matches in all competitions, winning just twice in their last seven. Jaissle and his players were booed off at half-time and again after the final whistle as the German coach begins to feel the heat in his first season in charge. Hired following Eddie Howe’s surprise close-season exit, former Red Bull Salzburg and Al-Ahli boss Jaissle has struggled to make an impact on Tyneside. Jaissle desperately needs a win at fellow strugglers Fulham on Saturday to ease the mounting scrutiny. Bizarrely, Newcastle have lost 22 of their last 33 Premier League matches on a Monday and many of their supporters headed for the exits well before the final whistle on a miserable rainy night. Barry’s eighth goal this season, including four in his last six matches, gave Everton their second win against Newcastle in the space of five days following their 3-1 victory in the League Cup fourth round on Thursday. Everton ended their run of two successive league defeats after losing against Arsenal and Chelsea. It was Everton’s first away league win since February 28 when they took three points on their previous visit to Newcastle. Jack Grealish was absent from the Everton squad for a second successive game after being axed for the Newcastle match last week due to a “breach of club discipline”. – Ramsey sees red – The on-loan Manchester City winger, who has been criticised for his off-field behaviour for much of his colourful career, reportedly skipped training prior to the League Cup clash. Everton said he was “not match fit” for the rematch with the Magpies, but his team coped just fine without him. Newcastle made a lively start and went close when Harvey Barnes fired just wide before Joelinton was narrowly off target from 25 yards. But chances were at a premium for both sides in a scrappy first half more notable for perspiration than inspiration. Everton’s opener four minutes after half-time was in keeping with the grimy fare that preceded it. Newcastle’s dismal marking let in Tyrique George for a shot that drew a weak save from Lukas Hornicek. Hornicek could only push it straight into the path of Barry for a simple tap-in that survived a lengthy VAR check for offside. It was a chance so easy that even the notoriously erratic Barry couldn’t fail to hit the target, although Newcastle were aggrieved by the VAR decision to let it stand. item.title: Tinubu fulfils WAFCON pledge, as Super Falcons players receive $100,000 each
item.description: The Federal Government has fulfilled President Bola Tinubu’s reward pledge to the Super Falcons following their historic 10th Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) title victory. The National Sports Commission (NSC) announced that the players, coaches and officials of the team had received their cash rewards in naira equivalent of $100,000 for each player and $50,000 for officials. The cash payments form part of the presidential reward package announced after the Super Falcons defeated their opponents to clinch their record-extending 10th WAFCON title. 𝙋𝙍𝙀𝙎𝙎 𝙍𝙀𝙇𝙀𝘼𝙎𝙀 The Federal Government, through the National Sports Commission (NSC), has fulfilled President @officialABAT Bola Ahmed Tinubu GCFR’s reward pledge to the Super Falcons @NGSuper_Falcons , with players, coaches and officials receiving their cash awards… pic.twitter.com/eGRfmA40HP — National Sports Commission (@NatSportsComm) November 2, 2026 In addition to the cash rewards, each of the players and officials had earlier received a three-bedroom flat in Abuja and the national honour of Officer of the Order of the Niger (OON). The commission celebrated the fulfilment of the presidential pledge, describing the timely disbursement of the rewards as recognition of the team’s contribution to Nigerian sports. Nigeria secured its 10th WAFCON title in July 2025 after defeating hosts Morocco 3-2 in the final, coming from two goals down to complete a remarkable comeback and maintain its dominance in African women’s football. The victory further extended the Super Falcons’ record as the most successful team in the history of the continental women’s competition. item.title: [VIDEO] Tinubu’s Aide Refutes Claim President Visited Saudi Arabia To Get Northern Votes
item.description: Senior Special Assistant to President Bola Tinubu on Foreign Affairs and Protocol, Ademola Oshodi, has dismissed claims that the President visited Mecca in Saudi Arabia to curry favour with northerners, ahead of the 2027 general elections. Oshodi, who stated this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday, said the trip was strictly religious as the President is a Muslim. The aide said that Tinubu’s presence in Mecca was not political, adding that even an opposition governor, Bala Mohammed of Bauchi State, was also present as a Muslim. He advised other presidential candidates in the 2027 general elections to also seek favour from God. The presidential aide said that though Nigerians are going through hardship, Tinubu is working to make things better. The President arrived in Saudi Arabia on October 29 and performed the religious rites associated with Umrah, seeking Allah’s guidance and blessings for Nigeria and its people. After completing the rites, he said that he felt fulfilled. Tinubu, who is the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential candidate in the 2027 general elections, also said that God has granted him the wisdom to continue to lead Nigerians. item.title: US VP says he, Trump feel ‘pretty good’ on prospect of deal with Iran
item.description: US Vice President JD Vance said Monday that he and President Donald Trump were optimistic about securing a deal with Iran, after Tehran revealed indirect negotiations with Washington. “The president and I both feel pretty good about the prospects for potentially coming to a negotiated settlement,” Vance told reporters. “We’ve certainly made some progress. We’ll see if we can make some more.” Vanguard News The post US VP says he, Trump feel ‘pretty good’ on prospect of deal with Iran appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: [VIDEO] Umrah: No Second Term Can Be Given To Anybody Via Spiritual Claim — Atiku’s Spokesperson
item.description: Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, has criticised President Bola Tinubu’s trip to Saudi Arabia for Umrah, saying a second term in office cannot be guaranteed via a spiritual claim. The spokesperson for the ADC presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, stated this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday. Shaibu said that visiting the holy land should be a personal affair and not national, accusing Tinubu’s supporters of politicising the event. ﻿ He questioned the President’s faith, saying former Kaduna State governor, Nasir El-Rufai, would not remain in custody if Tinubu had sincerity of faith. Shaibu also accused the President of speaking into a mic in Saudi Arabia while Nigerians “are dying of hunger”. He said that Tinubu administration’s claim that the economy has improved is false, as many Nigerians are facing hardship. According to him, Nigerians will remember Tinubu’s prayer in Mecca the same way they remember the high prices of food, goods and services. Asked whether Atiku would have accompanied Tinubu to Saudi Arabia if he had been invited, the aide said that the former vice president sponsored the President’s first trip to Mecca. On the chances of the ADC candidate in the 2027 presidential election across the northern states, Shaibu said Atiku is home and dry in the region. Tinubu departed Abuja for Makkah on October 29, where he performed the religious rites associated with Umrah, seeking Allah’s guidance and blessings for Nigeria and its people. Speaking shortly after completing the religious rites, which he described as a spiritual experience and an opportunity to pray for Nigeria, the President said he felt fulfilled. The All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential candidate in the 2027 general elections also said that God has granted him the wisdom to continue to lead Nigerians. “Well, I asked for wisdom and resilience to continue to serve the people. I know that has been granted. “Prior to the 2023 election, I did the same thing. I asked Allah to bless my Umrah then. He did, and I promised that I would come back to thank him, Almighty Allah. “There is no other God but him. He is the giver and the taker. “He owns the power. He said, ‘Use it well. If you don’t use it in accordance with my dictates, I can take it from you and give it to another person,’ Tinubu told journalists. “So, I have faith in that and believe extremely well that he has done me a favour to be the President of this great country.” The post [VIDEO] Umrah: No Second Term Can Be Given To Anybody Via Spiritual Claim — Atiku’s Spokesperson appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: N1.3 billion worth of property saved from fire in Nasarawa
item.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia Property worth N1.3 billion has been saved from destruction by fire in Nasarawa State, while assets valued at N2.1 billion were exposed to fire hazards. The incidents resulted in estimated property losses of N800 million and one recorded death. However, fire crews successfully rescued eight victims from life-threatening situations during the period. These figures were recorded across approximately 97 emergency calls received from January to date. This was revealed by the Nasarawa State Controller of Federal Fire Service (FFS) Commander of Fire, Eno Kelechi Nwachukwu, during the flag off ceremony of the 2026 National Fire Week Awareness Campaign, which took place on Monday at the Federal Secretariat Lafia, the Nasarawa State capital. In her opening speech, Nwachukwu reaffirms Fire Service commitment to maintaining rapid response capabilities, while urging residents, business owners, and market associations to prioritize fire safety precautions and report emergencies immediately to minimize casualties and property damage. She said ” Fire safety is not the responsibility of the Federal Fire Service alone, It is a collective responsibility that requires the active participation of government, private organizations, institutions, families, community leaders, and every individual”. Delivering this year’s address under the theme “Building a Fire Resilient Nigeria: One Community at a time, the State Controller of Federal Fire Service, highlighted the critical need to shift from reactive emergency responses to proactive, community-driven prevention strategies. Defining the vision of a fire-resilient nation, the State Controller described it as a state where families, schools, businesses, and industrial centers possess the awareness, capacity, and infrastructure needed to prevent disasters, respond effectively, and recover swiftly when emergencies occur. ​ The Fire Service chief warned against negligence, noting that fire disasters do not discriminate between government establishments, private residences, commercial markets, or places of worship. ​To mitigate risks, the Federal Fire Service announced an intensified public education drive focusing on common household and commercial hazards. ” Key priorities include educating community members on Safe handling and storage of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG/cooking gas, ​prevention of illegal and improper electrical connection​Curbing the indiscriminate burning of refuse​Proper storage of petroleum products and combustible materials ​She stressed that the nation’s overall security and economic stability begin at the local level, urging residence of the State to embrace safety standards in their daily activities to protect years of hard work, investments, and human lives. item.title: INEC pledges inclusive voting for PwDs
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has pledged to strengthen electoral accessibility for persons with disabilities (PwDs) ahead of the 2027 general elections. The commission said it would provide assistive materials, improve polling unit accessibility and train electoral officials to ensure inclusive participation. Gombe State Resident Electoral Commissioner, Alhaji Umar Gajiram, gave the assurance on Monday during a sensitisation workshop in Gombe. Gajiram, represented by the Administrative Secretary, Hajiya Fadimatu Bakari, said every Nigerian deserved equal opportunities to participate in democratic processes. He stressed that disability should never prevent eligible citizens from exercising their constitutional voting rights. According to him, INEC recognises that persons with disabilities have equal rights and that their votes, voices and contributions matter. He said the commission was implementing measures to remove barriers preventing PwDs from participating fully in elections. These include providing assistive materials, ensuring accessible polling units, training electoral officials and collaborating with disability organisations. Gajiram stressed that disability inclusion must be integrated into every electoral activity rather than treated as an additional responsibility. “Disability inclusion should not be treated as an additional responsibility but as an important part of our work,” he said. He urged Disability Desk Officers (DDOs) to maintain regular engagement with PwDs and communicate their challenges to the commission. He also encouraged participants to speak openly about their experiences and recommend improvements to electoral arrangements. “As we look forward to 2027, our goal is simple: to ensure that no eligible Nigerian is left out of the electoral process because of disability,” he said. He said INEC wanted wheelchair users to access polling units easily and visually impaired voters to receive appropriate assistance. Similarly, he said, persons with hearing impairments should have access to election information, enabling every eligible voter to participate with dignity and confidence. Also speaking, Gombe State Chairman of the Joint National Association of Persons with Disabilities (JONAPwD), Mallam Gambo Ahmad, commended INEC for organising the workshop. He described the arrangements as exceptional compared with previous engagements, particularly the provision of accessible communication materials. Ahmad specifically appreciated INEC for providing Braille materials for visually impaired participants and an interpreter for effective communication. He said the arrangements ensured participants could understand the discussions and contribute meaningfully to the proceedings. item.title: Video: ‘Let Toluwanisings have a befitting burial’ – Woli Arole makes appeal
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Comedian and preacher Woli Arole has appealed to those involved in the burial dispute surrounding late gospel singer Olayemi Bayonile Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, to allow him a befitting burial, urging them to end what he described as unnecessary public arguments. Arole made the appeal in a video shared on Instagram on Monday, describing the late singer as a great talent whose death had left friends and colleagues grieving. “I want to speak on behalf of Toluwanisings’ demise, and this is what God asked me to say. We’ve lost a great guy, a great gift to a generation. Even we, his friends and colleagues, have not recovered. For some of us, he is so close to us, and his death is really painful. A big elephant has gone,” he said. He also criticised people he accused of using the controversy to attract attention on social media, saying public discussion should instead focus on Toluwanisings’ wife and children. “It’s saddening and sad that a lot of people are now beginning to want to start to use it as a means for social media traction. You are m***. I have a right to say it. A young man had died in almost his prime, and the discussion is not even about the wife left behind and two kids? No. What you want to start doing is unlicensed, ungoverned, unnecessary talk, interviews and nonsense. A lot of people speaking about him this way never spoke about him while he was alive, about his music, please, please,” Arole said. He urged those involved to let the burial arrangements proceed and allow the singer to be laid to rest with dignity. “This is why it is a burden in my spirit, and I have to speak, and this is what the Lord is laying in my heart. The Bible says: Let the dead bury their dead. Whatever process, anything that needs to be done within that corner, let it be done. Let the young man be given a befitting burial,” he said. View this post on Instagram Woli Arole added that the burial dispute could not erase the singer’s musical legacy and called on the public to support his family and preserve his work through his children. “Nobody can ruin his legacy; he lived a good life, please. He sang songs that are eternal; his songs rang in our hearts. Whichever way he is buried, Toluwanisings is in our hearts forever; his sound is forever. So, please, I want to beg us in the name of Jesus, you should focus our energy on what is left: how his legacy will be preserved in his children and the wife,” he said. He concluded: “God bless Toluwanisings’ legacy, God bless his wife and his children, let the noise and unnecessary nonsense die down in the name of Jesus.” Toluwanisings’ family announced that the singer died in the early hours of October 14, 2026, but did not disclose the cause of death. The singer’s burial arrangements have drawn public attention following disagreements over where he should be laid to rest. item.title: NASS Considering Proposal To Create 74 Seats For Women, Says Bamidele
item.description: Leader of the Senate, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele, on Monday disclosed that the National Assembly Committee on the Review of the 1999 Constitution (as amended) had proposed the creation of 74 additional seats for women in the Senate and House of Representatives Bamidele, also Vice Chairman, Senate Committee on the Review of the 1999 Constitution, further revealed that the committee had proposed three additional seats in each State House of Assembly, all specifically reserved for women, without displacing any existing electoral seats. He made this disclosure at the 2026 Law Week organised by the International Federation of Women Lawyers (FIDA), Ekiti State Chapter on Monday, noting that the proposals were designed to deepen the inclusion of women in the country’s politics and governance process. A file photo of Senator Opeyemi Bamidele Ekiti FIDA, chaired by Mrs. Ayobami Olowoyo-Richards, organised the programme with the theme, “Justice in a Changing World: Responding to New Challenges Affecting Women and Children.” Bamidele attended the programme alongside the Chairman, House of Representatives Committee on Information and National Orientation, Steve Fatoba, and Speaker, Ekiti State House of Assembly, Adeoye Aribasoye, among others. “A Bill for an Act to alter the provisions of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 to provide for special seats for women in the National and State Houses of Assembly and for related matters is receiving our attention at the National Assembly,” Bamidele said. He further explained the centerpiece of the legislative initiative, which, according to him, was designed to create special seats for women at the National Assembly and State Houses of Assembly under the ongoing review of the 1999 Constitution. He added that the legislative initiative “is the fruit of extensive consultation and consensus-building. “It is why we commenced the constitutional amendment process early, ensuring that this is not a rushed, haphazard endeavour but a deliberate, inclusive, and thorough reform. “The proposal, as it stands, is meticulous in its design. It seeks to add 37 seats in the Senate and 37 seats in the House of Representatives. This suggests that if finally approved, each state of the federation, including FCT, will have one additional seat in each of the Houses of the National Assembly,” he added. Bamidele further revealed that the constitution review committee “has already proposed three additional seats for each state House of Assembly, all specifically reserved for women, without displacing any existing electoral seats. “This arrangement is proposed to run for a period of 16 years, four electoral cycles, before a comprehensive review.
